backcolor.problemsTitle: 1. How Many Pixel Shades Does an Image's Background Really Have?
backcolor.problem1: Product photos need white backgrounds, ID photos need blue backgrounds, social media avatars want a vibrant background — these tasks might take half an hour in Photoshop, while this tool only needs four steps: upload image, pick color, adjust tolerance, click apply. The Canvas API works at the pixel level, checking each pixel's color value and replacing background-matching pixels with the target color.
backcolor.problem2: The core difficulty of background replacement isn't 'changing color' but 'identifying which pixels belong to the background'. Solid-color backgrounds are simple — take the top-left pixel's color value and find all similar pixels. But real photo backgrounds often have lighting gradients, shadow transitions, edge mixing — this requires tolerance algorithms to define 'how close counts as the same color'. This tool's tolerance slider is based on the CIE76 color distance formula, more aligned with human perception than simple RGB Euclidean distance.
backcolor.problem3: Everything happens entirely in the browser — images are never uploaded to any server. Based on Canvas getImageData/putImageData for pixel-level operations, processing speed directly relates to image resolution. A 1920x1080 photo typically completes background replacement in 1-2 seconds.
backcolor.formatTitle: 2. Tolerance: The Ruler That Decides 'Which Pixels Are Background'
backcolor.formatJpg: JPG Format Note: JPG is a lossy compression format — solid-color backgrounds produce subtle color block noise after compression (e.g., a pure white background actually contains #FEFFFE, #FFFDFB and other tiny variations). Recommend adjusting tolerance to 10-20 to cover these noise pixels, otherwise the replaced background will show 'spots'.
backcolor.formatPng: PNG Format Advantage: PNG supports alpha channel (transparency). This tool can replace backgrounds with complete transparency — this is the core principle of background removal. Transparency-replaced PNGs can be overlaid on any background, making them the preferred solution for e-commerce product images and UI design.
backcolor.formatGif: GIF Format Limitation: GIF only supports 256-color palette. After background replacement, colors are quantized to the nearest palette color, which may cause color shifts. Animated GIFs only process the first frame.
backcolor.featuresTitle: 3. How Canvas Pixel-Level Color Replacement Works

backcolor.featurePreview: Smart Edge Transition: Simple binary judgment produces jagged edges. This tool uses alpha blending at color boundaries — the farther a pixel is from the background color, the lower the replacement degree, creating natural transitions.
backcolor.featureExport: 8 Preset Colors + Custom Color Picker: Built-in white, black, red, green, blue, cyan, magenta, yellow — 8 common background colors. Custom color picker supports entering any HEX color value for brand color matching.

compressor.algorithmTip:
There is no single best compression algorithm - only the strategy that best fits your needs. Different algorithms suit different scenarios:
- Default compression: Balances quality and size while preserving the original image format. Not suitable for transparent PNG images. Recommended for: regular JPG images and non-transparent images that must keep their original format
- Lossless compression: Preserves the highest quality and original extension. Not recommended for JPG images, as it may enlarge files or fail to compress effectively. Recommended for: transparent PNG images and images requiring full detail retention
- Aggressive compression: Prioritizes smaller file size and converts everything to JPG for the best compression ratio, noticeably reducing image quality. Recommended for: minimizing file size when image quality is not a priority
- WebP format: An efficient modern browser image format that significantly reduces file size while keeping high quality. Recommended for: website images, WebP-supported apps, and when seeking a balance of high quality and small size
compressor.qualityTip: The higher the compression quality, the better the image quality but the larger the file size; the lower the value, the higher the compression ratio but image details may be lost. A setting between 70-90 is recommended; adjust according to your actual needs.
compressor.dimensionTip: Tip: Max dimension limits the upper bound of the image (100-16384px); max file size limits the size of the compressed file, ranging from 20KB up to the original file size - you can enter any value within this range.
compressor.infoIntro: Image Compression: Finding the Optimal Balance Between Quality and File Size
compressor.problemsTitle: 1. Why You Need a Professional Image Compression Tool
compressor.problem1: Phone photos are easily 5-10MB each, uploading to websites is painfully slow; dozens of product images on an e-commerce detail page add up to over 100MB, and pages loading over 3 seconds lose 40% of users. Image compression isn't simply 'reducing quality' — it's shrinking file size by 60%-90% while maintaining nearly imperceptible visual difference.
compressor.problem2: This tool uses the Canvas API to re-encode images — precisely controlling compression degree by adjusting quality parameters (0.1-1.0). Real-time display of original size, compressed size, compression ratio, and dimension info. Batch compression support — upload multiple images at once, set unified parameters, then one-click batch compress and package download.
compressor.problem3: All processing is done locally in the browser, images are never uploaded to any server. E-commerce sellers, social media operators, and front-end developers can greatly improve work efficiency — batch processing 20 product images typically takes only 10-20 seconds.
compressor.formatTitle: 2. What the Compression Algorithms Are Doing
compressor.formatJpg: JPEG Compression: JPEG uses Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to convert the image from spatial domain to frequency domain, then heavily quantizes high-frequency components (details insensitive to human eyes) — this is the essence of 'lossy compression'. The quality parameter controls how aggressive the quantization is.
compressor.formatPng: PNG Compression: PNG uses the DEFLATE algorithm (LZ77 + Huffman coding), which is lossless compression. Compression space mainly comes from color simplification: reducing 24-bit true color to fewer color depths. Compression ratio is usually not as good as JPEG (typically 20%-50%), but no pixel information is lost.
compressor.formatWebp: WebP: A modern image format developed by Google, based on VP8 video encoding. 25-35% smaller than JPG at equivalent quality, while supporting transparency and animation.

convert.problem1: JPG is great for photos but can't handle transparency, PNG supports transparency but has large file sizes, WebP does both but older systems don't recognize it, GIF is limited to 256 colors but can make animations, BMP is lossless but huge, ICO is specifically for website favicons — choose the wrong format and you'll end up with bloated files slowing down web pages, lost alpha channels causing white edges, or incompatible display on target platforms.

convert.formatDescJpg: JPG/JPEG: The most universal lossy compressed image format, ideal for photos and color-rich images. No alpha channel support; compressed file sizes are small. The go-to format for web display, social media sharing, and email attachments. Note: Repeated saving (multiple lossy compression passes) causes cumulative quality degradation.
convert.formatDescPng: PNG: Lossless compression format that perfectly preserves every pixel's original data. Supports Alpha transparency channel (semi-transparent effects), making it the best choice for icons, logos, screenshots, and UI designs. File size is typically 2-5x larger than JPG, but there are no compression artifacts. Recommended for scenarios requiring transparent backgrounds or repeated editing.
convert.formatDescWebp: WebP: A modern image format developed by Google, supporting both lossy and lossless compression. At equivalent quality, file sizes are 25-35% smaller than JPG and 26% smaller than PNG. Supports alpha channel and animation. Supported by Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and other modern browsers, but some older Safari and IE versions are not compatible.
convert.formatDescGif: GIF: A legacy image format supporting animation, with up to 256 colors per frame. Suitable for simple animations and memes, not ideal for photo-type images (limited colors cause poor quality). File size is proportional to frame count and dimensions — controlling parameters can effectively reduce size.
convert.formatDescBmp: BMP: The native bitmap format for Windows, uncompressed (or only supporting simple RLE compression). File size is typically 5-10x that of equivalent JPGs. Mainly used for scenarios requiring lossless preservation of original pixel data, such as print plate-making and medical imaging. For daily use, convert to PNG or JPG.

edit.usageColorDetect: CSS Filter vs Canvas Pixel Operations: Real-time preview uses CSS filter (GPU-accelerated, extremely fast but doesn't modify pixels); applying operations uses Canvas pixel operations (CPU computation, modifies actual pixel data). edit.usagePixelReplace: Convolution Operations: Blur and sharpen filters are essentially convolution operations — sliding a small numeric matrix (kernel) across the image, where each pixel's new value equals a weighted sum of surrounding pixels. eyedropper.problemsTitle: 1. The Color You See May Not Be the Real Color
eyedropper.problem1: A designer sees a beautiful button color on a website and wants to reuse it in their project — screenshot, open in PS, eyedropper tool, read color value... the workflow is too heavy. A front-end developer wants to replicate the color scheme from a design, guessing colors from an image? Off by one shade level and the entire visual feel changes. This tool lets you click anywhere on an image to instantly get that pixel's exact color value — HEX, RGB, HSL displayed simultaneously.
eyedropper.problem2: The color picker is based on Canvas's getImageData API — directly reading RGBA values at specified coordinates from the image's pixel data. Precision reaches pixel level; there's no 'visual estimation' error. The magnifier lets you precisely locate exactly which pixel — especially in edge areas, where a one-pixel deviation can lead to a completely different color.
eyedropper.problem3: Besides single-point picking, it also supports area picking — select a rectangular region and the tool calculates the average color of all pixels within it. This is particularly useful for getting the dominant tone of gradient backgrounds and the overall color tendency of blurred areas.

gif.problemsTitle: 1. GIF Animation Creation Is Far More Complex Than You Imagine
gif.problem1: The GIF format was born in 1987, nearly 40 years ago — yet it remains the most popular animation format on the internet. Emoji stickers, product demos, tutorial steps, data visualization animations — GIFs are everywhere. But making GIFs isn't simple: arranging multiple images in order, setting each frame's display duration, handling frame transitions, optimizing file size — traditional methods require Photoshop's timeline feature or professional animation software.
gif.problem2: This tool makes GIF creation extremely simple: upload image sequences (supports JPG/PNG/WebP), set each frame's duration (0.1-10 seconds), preview animation effects, one-click generate GIF file. Supports adjusting output size (scaling) and quality (color count), finding balance between file size and image quality.
gif.problem3: Based on the gif.js library, GIF encoding is completed in the browser — using Web Worker for parallel frame data processing, without blocking the main thread. Generated GIFs can be previewed and downloaded directly. The entire process doesn't upload to any server.
gif.formatGif: Lossless but Limited: GIF uses LZW lossless compression — consecutive same-color pixels within a frame are efficiently compressed. This is why solid-color animations (like text animations) have much smaller files than complex photo animations — the former has many consecutive identical pixels, the latter has nearly every pixel different.
gif.featureOnline: Frame Duration Control: Each frame's display time (unit: seconds), range 0.1-10 seconds. 0.1s/frame = 10 FPS (smooth animation), 0.2s/frame = 5 FPS (slideshow effect), 0.5s/frame = 2 FPS (slow display). Total duration = frame count × per-frame duration.
gif.featurePreview: Real-time Preview: After uploading frame images, plays in loop preview at the set frame duration. Preview updates immediately when adjusting frame duration — no need to regenerate the GIF to see the effect.
gif.featureExport: Output Size Scaling: Original frame images may be scaled down before writing to GIF — scaling can greatly reduce file size (halving width reduces total pixels by 75%). Recommended: animation width should not exceed 480px (social media friendly size).
gif.featureSecurity: Web Worker Parallel Encoding: GIF encoding is CPU-intensive — gif.js uses Web Worker to distribute encoding work to background threads, keeping the main thread responsive. 10 frames at 480px typically completes encoding in 3-5 seconds.

gif.noteSecurity1: The GIF encoding engine runs in the browser's Web Worker thread based on the gif.js library. Decoding, scaling, palette generation, frame composition, and all other computations for multi-frame images are completed on the local CPU with zero network communication throughout. Even when composing screenshot animations containing commercial sensitive information, image data is never leaked.
gif.noteSecurity2: Uploaded source images and in-progress GIF frame data are only temporarily stored in the browser's Worker memory. After closing the tab, Worker threads terminate immediately, and all image data and intermediate frame caches are destroyed from memory. The tool does not use any persistent storage mechanism (localStorage, IndexedDB, etc.) to save images.
gif.noteSecurity3: When creating GIF tutorials or demos containing internal company system screenshots, unreleased product interfaces, customer data, and other sensitive content, using browser incognito mode is recommended. Incognito mode ensures browsing history, DNS cache, temporary files, etc. are thoroughly cleared after closing, preventing sensitive screenshot remnants.
gif.noteLimit1: The GIF format was born in 1987, with each frame supporting at most 256 colors (8-bit palette) — this is an inherent limitation of the format itself. After compositing photos (millions of colors) into a GIF, colors are quantized to a 256-color palette, causing color simplification and banding. If you need high color fidelity animation, consider WebP animation or APNG format.
gif.noteLimit2: Supports up to 5 images for one-frame GIF composition; for larger quantities, process in batches.
gif.noteLimit3: Maximum output width is 800px; for larger sizes, use the cropping tool first.
gif.noteLimit4: GIF file size is proportional to frame count, dimensions, and color complexity — control parameters to reduce size.
gif.noteDelay2: Product display/step demo: 300-500ms, 2-3 frames per second, comfortable viewing.
gif.noteDelay3: Slideshow/slow transition: 1000-2000ms, suitable for tutorials and image-text display.
gif.notePerf1: Generating GIF from large images may take a while; please be patient.
gif.notePerf2: Do not close the browser or refresh the page during generation.
gif.notePerf3: It is recommended to compress images before generating to improve processing speed.
gif.notePerf4: GIF file size depends on frame count, dimensions, and color count.
gif.noteFaq1: Color distortion after generation: GIF format only supports 256 colors/frame — this is a format limitation, not a tool issue.
gif.noteFaq2: Animation too fast/slow: Adjust the frame delay value. Smaller value = faster animation, larger value = slower.
gif.noteFaq3: GIF file too large: Reduce image count, lower output width, or increase frame delay.
gif.noteFaq4: Generation failed: Check if image format is supported; single images should not exceed 10MB.
gif.formatJpg: 256-Color Palette Limitation: Each frame of GIF can use at most 256 colors. For color-rich photos, this means color quantization is necessary — selecting the most visually representative 256 colors from millions. This tool uses the Median Cut algorithm for color quantization, preserving the visually most important colors.
gif.formatPng: Inter-Frame Optimization: GIF supports two storage modes — each frame stores all pixels completely, or only stores changes relative to the previous frame (inter-frame optimization). The latter can significantly reduce file size, but requires minimal changes between frames. This tool uses inter-frame optimization by default, which can be disabled in settings.
gif.usageClickUpload: Batch Upload: Click or drag to upload multiple images (2-100). Filenames are auto-sorted — ensure upload order is the frame order. Supports JPG/PNG/WebP.
gif.usageFormats: Frame Image Requirements: All frames should have consistent dimensions — if not, the tool auto-scales to the first frame's size. PNG frame transparency becomes white in GIF (GIF transparency is boolean, doesn't support semi-transparency).

gif.usageColorValue: Quality Setting: Range 1-30, 1 is best quality (most colors), 30 is fastest (fewest colors). Recommended balanced value: 10-15.

gif.usageToleranceLarge: Generate GIF: Click "Generate" to start encoding. Progress bar shows encoding progress. Within 10 frames usually completes in 5 seconds; 50 frames may need 20-30 seconds.

gif.usageColorDetect: Color Quantization: Collects all pixel colors from all frames, uses Median Cut algorithm to generate a global palette (max 256 colors). Each frame's pixel colors are mapped to the nearest color in the palette.
gif.usagePixelReplace: LZW Compression: Each frame's index data (each pixel represented by palette index) is compressed using LZW algorithm — consecutive identical index sequences are encoded as short codes.
gif.usageEdge: Inter-Frame Optimization: Compares pixel differences between adjacent frames, only stores changed areas (disposal method marked by graphic control extension blocks). Static background is stored only once; subsequent frames only record foreground changes.

watermark-remove.intro: Remove watermarks, text, and other obstructions from images, supporting multiple image formats
watermark-remove.uploadText: Click or drag to upload images

watermark-remove.infoIntro: Watermark Removal: Algorithmically Repair Obscured Image Areas
watermark-remove.problemsTitle: 1. The Essence of Watermark Removal Is 'Image Inpainting'
watermark-remove.problem1: Preview images downloaded from stock photo sites have watermarks, old photos have unwanted text overlays, screenshots accidentally contain personal information — these scenarios all require removing watermarks or text from images. But watermark removal isn't simply 'erasing' — erasing leaves blank areas that need to be 'filled back' with surrounding pixels. This is the 'Image Inpainting' problem in computer vision.
watermark-remove.problem2: This tool provides 6 removal methods: Smart Fill (surrounding pixel interpolation), Blur (Gaussian blur covering), Mosaic (pixelated covering), Feather Edges (edge blending), Color Overlay (solid color covering), Median Blur (median filter). Each method has adjustable parameters for fine-tuning the removal effect.
watermark-remove.problem3: All processing is done in the browser; images are never uploaded to any server. Supports batch processing — upload multiple images, draw removal areas, one-click batch process and download.
watermark-remove.formatJpg: Smart Fill: Analyzes pixels around the watermark area and uses interpolation algorithms to fill the region, matching the surrounding texture and color. Best for complex backgrounds where the watermark needs to blend naturally.
watermark-remove.formatPng: Blur & Mosaic: Blur applies Gaussian blur to the watermark area, making content unreadable while maintaining color continuity. Mosaic divides the area into pixelated blocks, completely obscuring the original content. Both are ideal for privacy protection rather than content restoration.
watermark-remove.formatWebp: Feather Edges & Color Overlay: Feather blends the watermark area edges with surrounding pixels for a smooth transition. Color Overlay covers the area with a specified solid color. Both work best on simple or uniform backgrounds.
watermark-remove.featureOnline: Multi-Region Support: Can add multiple removal areas simultaneously, each independently configured. Areas are displayed as draggable, resizable rectangles on the image.
watermark-remove.featurePreview: Real-time Preview: After applying removal, the result is immediately visible. Compare before and after to verify the effect.

resizer.intro: Online image resizer supporting custom dimensions and presets, aspect ratio lock, multiple output formats, original and result side-by-side preview

resizer.infoIntro: Image Resizing: Precise Control Over Every Pixel of Output Dimensions
resizer.problemsTitle: 1. Why You Can't Just Drag the Corner to Resize
resizer.problem1: The built-in image viewer on your OS can resize images — but its algorithm uses simple nearest-neighbor interpolation. Shrinking produces jagged edges and moiré patterns, while enlarging results in a blurry mess. More importantly, it doesn't support setting output dimensions by exact pixel values — you can't tell it 'I want this image to be exactly 800x600 pixels'.
resizer.problem2: This tool provides three resizing modes: Exact Dimensions (enter target width and height in pixels), Ratio Scaling (50%, 25%, etc.), and Preset Sizes (desktop resolutions, mobile resolutions, social media dimensions, etc.). The scaling algorithm uses Canvas bilinear interpolation, which preserves more detail and reduces jagged edges when shrinking images.
resizer.problem3: Batch resizing is supported — upload multiple images, set a uniform target size, and process them all with one click, then download as a package. All processing is done in the browser; images are never uploaded to any server. Ideal for e-commerce sellers batch-producing product images, front-end developers generating thumbnails, and similar scenarios.
resizer.formatInput: Exact Dimensions Mode: Enter target width and height directly in pixels. If 'Keep Aspect Ratio' is checked, only one dimension is needed and the other is calculated automatically. If unchecked, width and height can be set freely — which may cause distortion (stretching or compressing), suitable for scenarios requiring strict size matching.
resizer.formatOutput: Ratio Scaling Mode: Scale by percentage — 50% means both width and height are halved (total pixels reduced to 1/4), 200% means both dimensions double. Common ratios: 200% (double size), 100% (original), 50% (half size), 25% (thumbnail).
resizer.featuresTitle: 3. Technical Details of the Scaling Algorithm
resizer.featureCustom: Bilinear Interpolation: Canvas drawImage uses bilinear interpolation by default — each pixel's color in the target image is the weighted average of the nearest 2×2 pixel area in the source image. Much smoother than nearest-neighbor, much faster than bicubic — the optimal balance for image resizing.
resizer.featureRatio: Real-time Size Preview: After uploading, original dimensions and file size are displayed. Target size adjustments update the preview in real time — including estimated output file size (based on total pixels and target format).
resizer.featurePreset: Aspect Ratio Lock: Checked by default. When width changes, height adjusts proportionally and vice versa. Uncheck for free width/height control — ideal for specific dimension needs like avatars (200×200).
resizer.featureFormat: Batch Processing: Set a uniform target size for multiple images and process them with one click. Each image is resized independently — images with different original sizes can all be resized to the same target dimensions.
resizer.featureSecurity: Format + Quality Control: Convert formats and adjust output quality while resizing — complete all optimization in a single operation.

resizer.usageRealPreview: Quality Note: Shrinking images usually yields excellent quality (redundant information decreases), while enlarging may show slight blur — an inherent limitation of all interpolation algorithms.
resizer.usagePrincipleCanvas: Canvas Resizing: Uses Canvas drawImage method for high-quality image scaling.
resizer.usagePrincipleAntiAlias: Shrink Algorithm: Each target pixel corresponds to a region of source pixels (e.g., scaling from 1920 to 960, each target pixel maps to a 2×2 source pixel area). Bilinear interpolation calculates the weighted average of these 4 pixels — weights determined by the target pixel's exact position within the source area.
resizer.usagePrincipleLossless: Enlarge Algorithm: Each target pixel maps to a sub-pixel position in the source — bilinear interpolation estimates the color value from the nearest 2×2 source pixels. Smoother than nearest-neighbor, but softer than bicubic.
resizer.usageEdge: File Size Estimation: For JPG output, file size is roughly proportional to total pixel count (at the same quality setting). Halving the width reduces file size to about 1/4. PNG compression also depends on image content — solid color areas compress better.
resizer.noteSecurity1: Image resizing is performed directly in the browser via Canvas 2D API drawImage method — the source image is decoded, redrawn on Canvas at target dimensions, then encoded to the specified output format. The entire resizing process (including pixel resampling and anti-aliasing) runs entirely on the local CPU, with no network requests or third-party services required.
resizer.noteSecurity2: Original and resized images are stored only as Blob URLs in browser memory. Closing the tab or refreshing the page immediately releases all image data from JavaScript heap memory. The tool does not use Cookie, localStorage, or IndexedDB to persist any image data. When processing commercial product images or confidential materials, using incognito mode is recommended.
resizer.noteSecurity3: When resizing commercial materials (unreleased product renders, internal data visualization screenshots) or images containing sensitive information (dashboard screenshots, financial reports), incognito mode is recommended. Incognito mode ensures the browser retains no browsing history or cache files, thoroughly clearing all traces when closed, providing maximum commercial privacy protection.
resizer.noteSize1: Shrinking Images (Recommended): Quality is basically unaffected — Canvas drawImage uses bilinear interpolation for pixel downsampling, producing smooth natural edges. File size decreases significantly with reduced dimensions (roughly proportional to total pixel count). This is the most common use case for web optimization and image sharing.
resizer.noteSize2: Enlarging Images (Use with Caution): Cannot add detail that doesn't exist in the original. Large magnification (e.g., 200×200 to 1000×1000) will show blur and artifacts — the algorithm can only estimate new pixel colors through interpolation. Always use the original large image for shrinking rather than enlarging a small one. If enlarging is necessary, consider AI super-resolution tools.
resizer.noteSize3: Keep Aspect Ratio: Strongly recommended to keep checked; otherwise the image will be stretched and distorted. Unchecking allows free input of any width/height values.
resizer.noteFormat1: JPG: Smallest file size, ideal for photos and web images, does not support transparency.
resizer.noteFormat2: PNG: Lossless format, supports transparent backgrounds, ideal for icons and screenshots, larger files.
resizer.noteFormat3: WebP: Modern format, 25-35% smaller than JPG with transparency support, all modern browsers compatible.
resizer.noteFaq1: Blurry after enlarging: This is an inherent limitation of image processing — enlarging cannot recover original detail. Use the original high-resolution image and shrink to target size instead.
resizer.noteFaq2: How to resize to a specific file size: This tool controls pixel dimensions, not file size directly. You can indirectly control it by adjusting output format and quality.
resizer.noteFaq3: Aspect ratio is off after resizing: Make sure 'Keep Aspect Ratio' is checked, then modify only width or height — the other will adjust automatically.
resizer.noteFaq4: Does it support animated GIF: Only the first frame of GIF is processed; animation effects will be lost.
